recognize_zh: 化療後骨髓顆粒中造血細胞稀少，主要是脂肪空泡、淡紫色基質、梭形基質細胞與含深色含鐵血黃素顆粒的巨噬細胞，僅殘留少數巨核細胞，呈現骨髓低細胞、以間質為主的治療後變化。
features: Marrow particle composed largely of fat vacuoles and pale purple stromal ground substance
Markedly reduced hematopoietic precursors within the particle
Spindled and stellate stromal cells with streaming nuclei
Macrophages containing dark coarse hemosiderin/debris granules
A few residual large megakaryocytes and scattered small lymphoid or plasma cells
No clusters of blasts identified in this field
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a particle composed predominantly of fat and stromal elements, including spindled stromal cells, pale ground substance and macrophages laden with dark pigment granules. Hematopoietic precursors are markedly reduced, with only a few residual megakaryocytes and scattered small mononuclear cells; no aggregates of blasts are seen. Findings are consistent with a hypocellular, stroma-rich post-chemotherapy marrow; assessment of residual disease requires a trephine biopsy for cellularity and flow cytometry or molecular studies.

ddx.vs: Shows a similarly fat- and stroma-rich hypocellular particle, so the distinction depends on the history of cytotoxic therapy rather than morphology.
Would show dysplastic residual hematopoiesis or clusters of blasts, which require high-power review, CD34 immunostaining and flow cytometry to exclude.
Features abundant amorphous pink-purple extracellular mucopolysaccharide material with fat atrophy, typically in cachexia, rather than cellular stroma with pigment-laden macrophages.
